content:
Use the Test-First Fixer workflow. Bug found by a headless-browser smoke check (not by our unit tests): after the spoken-reminders change, the app breaks on load. The browser console shows:
  ReferenceError: Cannot access 'speechInterval' before initialization
and because index.js stops there, the settings, statistics and tasks buttons no longer open anything. All 92 unit tests still pass, so our test suite has a blind spot: nothing ever loads index.js.

1. First close the blind spot: write test/boot.test.js (node:test, no dependencies) that boots the real app scripts in a node:vm context with a stub browser: a recursive Proxy-based stub that returns callable stubs for any property (document.getElementById, querySelector, classList, style, addEventListener, matchMedia, Worker, indexedDB.open, navigator, Notification, etc.), a real in-memory localStorage (getItem/setItem/removeItem) pre-seeded with pomo-version "1" and two tasks, and timers that do not run. Load, in the same order as index.html, every local <script src> (read index.html and extract them so new scripts are picked up automatically), then index.js. The test asserts that booting throws no error. Also add a second test that boots with an EMPTY localStorage (first visit). Run npm test and show that the boot test FAILS with the ReferenceError above.
2. Fix the root cause in index.js with the smallest change: the speech settings variables are read by setTime() during start-up before their `let` declarations run. Move the speech state declarations (speechInterval, speechTransitions) up next to the other timer state near the top of index.js (keep the DOM wiring where it is), or guard their use; pick the cleaner one and explain.
3. Run npm test until everything is green, including the boot tests.
4. While you are there: check whether anything else that setTime(), nextRound() or focusEnd() reads is declared with let/const later in the file than its first possible call during start-up (cite file:line). Report what you find; fix only real problems.
One simple command per execute_command call.
